lines.en: : Hello everyone and welcome back from our not-so-brief commercial break!

: Unfortunately, we were unable to obtain permission from Touka to film inside of her building, so “Familial Face-Off!” will forever be un-aired and no one but the girls involved will ever know how it went down!
: Which, given the circumstances and how it involved children, is probably for the best.

: That said, I’m joined here now by a different child! Because this is apparently what my life is like now. And it’s definitely not strange at all that she isn’t related to any of the girls in class but is still here anyway!
: Say “Hi,” Nao-chan! Oh, wait! You can’t! Which definitely does not add one more layer of responsibility into the picture that should otherwise just not exist at all! Hooray!
: Oh! It looks like Nao-chan has something to say after all! But what could it-
: So that’s how it’s gonna be, huh?
: Somebody needs to just buy you a tablet already. I’ll see if I can get Touka to pick one up for you.

: But before that, we do have two more contests left before we wrap things up for the day! And given that this one will be our last televised contest until tomorrow, here’s hoping we can make it a good one!
: The rules are simple. You’ll each have twenty minutes to draw a picture of “something you like.”
: And by “draw,” I mean actually draw. None of that generative AI crap that people are trying to pass off as art lately. You feel me?
: How exactly would we put that on paper to begin with?
: Hell if I know. They’re coming out with new tech every day now and I ain’t getting any younger. Only a matter of time until we’ve got collapsible printers or something.
: You heard the kid. Or didn’t. No penguins.
: And what’s the problem with penguins exactly?

: They are one of the ten most sinful birds of all, and exist primarily in places the light cannot touch. Plus, the way they recycle sustenance has not been approved by God. It defies all that is holy and just!
: Their uncanny waddle has little to do with their feet and everything to do with the burden they carry on their avian shoulders. They must be avoided at all costs.
: Okay, cool. I’ll gladly agree to whatever gets me away from this child quicker as I’m not looking to be dragged through dimensions again. Can we start?
: Dragged through dimensions? You on a Vonnegut kick or something?
: Come back to reality and learn to separate fiction from it or you’ll wind up like Molly. I don’t need two people asking me to guest-voice NPCs on a weekly basis. I’m busy enough as-is.
: Okay. Well, I’m going to go sit down and wait for the timer to start. I imagine I’ll need at least ten minutes to think of something I like in the first place.
: Just draw a watermelon or something. It’ll be easier to accomplish that within the alloted time than whatever sketch of God Yasu is going to try and do.
: God can not be drawn, for His figure on paper would set the world ablaze. I also need time to think of something else I like...
: Right. Well, I don’t speak wizard, but I’m pretty sure Nao-chan is telling you two to just give it your all or whatever because that’s what would make sense in the context of this situation.
: So yeah, she and I will just hang out over here while you two do your thing and try not to be distracted by your “fans.”
: Fans? But I-
: Surprise! Ayane came here with me to cheer you on!
: Just Ami barely made it since her contest ran late. Which she won, by the way. So you can mark that down in your notes, Miss Imai.
: Oh, good. I was worried she was going to kill one of them.
: I’m right here...
: Molly and I came to cheer you on as well, Yasu.
: Message received, by the way. I will tone down on the handing out of side quests if you feel that strongly about not voicing my NPCs.
: Touka! Emerald Guardian! I’m so very excited to see you!
: And I’m so very excited to be done with all of this.
: There’s a man I need to say some very unkind words to in a hotel right now. And each moment I spend here is one more moment I am not spending making him feel bad for the things he has done to me.
: Those “things” being what, exactly?
: You’re off the clock, Miss Imai. It isn’t exactly appropriate to be asking students about their personal lives right now, is it?
: Take a seat, horse girl. There ain’t a second I’m off the clock so long as y’all are my students. Maya-

: Nothing inappropriate has ever happened between he and I and, if it sounded as if that is what I was insinuating, it’s a complete misunderstanding. Conversation over. Any further questions will be invading my personal space.
: Tch...fine. Time starts now. Begin!
: You sounded awfully prepared to make that statement, Maya. How long have you been practicing?
: That depends. Which number would make you most jealous of the amount of sex I’ve had with your father?
: Miss Imai could still be listening, you know.
: Let her. Worst case scenario is that it destroys Sensei’s reputation and causes his relationship with Niki to go up in flames.
: Isn’t that the best case scenario for you?
: No. The best case scenario is that Miss Imai approves and Niki just dies. But I can’t see how this could ever possibly lead to that, so I doubt it will happen.
: Ignoring how none of these hypotheticals seem even remotely likely, what are you planning on drawing? I feel like I haven’t seen your art in years.
: Yeah, you used to draw manga all the time for the club. What happened to that?
: Nothing but misery and an array of missed opportunities to express myself in ways better suited to my tastes.
: Then maybe you can express it this time by sketching my dad’s penis or something? You’ve certainly seen it enough.
: I have too, so I could confirm the artistic accuracy of such a drawing. I have a hard time thinking it could win Maya the competition, though.
: I don’t know about that, honestly. It’s a very impressive penis and I’m sure Miss Imai likes it too.
: I think I might just do a self-portrait.
: Yeah, that tracks.
: Hey, Maya? If you’re so confident and conceited and stuff, how come you always get so pissed off and whiny or start crying whenever Niki comes up?
: On second thought, I think I might actually do a sketch of Ami falling off of a building.
: This is so hard! All of the things I like are so hard to draw!
: Well, Yasu, that’s because you like a total of one thing. And that thing just happens to be a fictional entity beyond human comprehension.
: Objection! The Priestess of Fallen Snow cares for more than just her patron now, for she has discovered the great world of manga.

: So what you’re saying is that she’s finally developed a new hobby and that it’s merely just a waste of time. Excellent work, Molly. It was certainly the right idea leaving her in your hands after school hours.
: Well, what would you rather her enjoy instead? A hobby is a hobby and people should just do what they like, no?
: I’d be happier if Yasu’s interest became rooted in more refined hobbies. Like ikebana or horseback riding.
: Great. I’ll just show her Uma Musume then and we can both win.
: Uma...Musume?
: You live in the land of the rising sun and don’t know about Uma Musume? How is that even possible?
: I...don’t keep up with modern trends! I have no idea what-

: It’s a game where they turned a bunch of famous horses into cute girls that you can train and race with! And if that’s what it takes to suck you into the world of otaku culture, I will beat you over the head with it until you submit.
: P...Preposterous! To take something so...honorable and turn it into a...more than likely sexualized mockery of a respectable pastime is just...that...uh...
: Wh...What was it called again?
: Uma Musume.
: Right! Despicable. I’ve never been less interested in anything in my life.
: Touka-
: Yasu! If you can’t think of anything else to draw, sketch a horse! To distract me.
: From what?
: Anger, obviously. Not even the rich are safe from peasant culture these days. Unbelievable. Yasu! Horse. Now.
: You want me to draw a horse from memory?! But I have no idea what they look like!
: What do you mean you have no idea what they look like?! You see them at the manor all the time!
: But they’re so big and scary! And I’m not supposed to look them in the face, so I normally just close my eyes and wait until you’re done talking to them!
: You talk to your horses?
: At least they exist! Unlike whatever nonsense the two of you talk to.
: I mostly just talk to my friends now.
: Well...good for you. But my friends happen to be horses and there is nothing wrong with or lonely about that.
: Why do I feel like the cool one this time? That never happens.
: I...can try? But you have to promise to not get mad at me if it looks bad.
: I won’t be mad. Just extremely disappointed.
: That...isn’t much better...
: Okay, I think I’ve got it. I know what to draw.
: Are you not going to do the watermelon like Imani suggested?
: Of course not. That’s not nearly impressive or ambitious enough and this is a rare opportunity for me to show off without coming across as overbearing.
: Maya, you have twenty minutes.
: Closer to fifteen now, actually.
: Yeah, and nothing has happened yet. So-
: Just leave. You being here is nothing but a distraction anyway. So if you actually want me to win this in order to get Sensei as a slave-
: Why does everyone keep saying that? The rules said nothing about him becoming a slave. Just that we-
: Let’s just go wait outside. If Maya thinks being alone will help her win, we’ll let her be alone.
: I mean, she’ll probably win regardless of what she draws. I think our presence is just preventing her from showing off as greatly as she wants to.
: Either way! Our fate is in your hands now, Maya. Don’t mess it up. Win us back my dad or-
: Blah, blah, blah. I obviously don’t intend to lose. But I’d like to try and win Sensei back in my own way by drawing something for him.

: So if you two plan to sit here and ruin my chances of that because you’re afraid he’ll want to run away with me after he receives it, I will take this pencil and jam it so deep into your trachea that you’ll have no choice but to-
: Sleep.
: I’m not tired, though.
: You’ve been awake for over twenty-four hours. You need to-
: You don’t need to stick around if you have to get home. It’s not like I’m going anywhere.
: It’s not about you going anywhere. It’s about you not taking care of yourself and...what are you drawing?
: Ami.
: So I don’t forget what she looks like since you won’t let me back in your house.
: Maya-
: I don’t need an explanation. We’ve already talked about how important it is that I remain a secret.
: It’d be nice, though....if that weren’t the case. If she and I could be friends one day.
: Are you feeling lonely? Trapped in here like this?
: Not at all. I’ve always wanted to see Stockholm. I just never thought I’d get to do it from the safety of my room.
: Our room. I live here too.
: You live two lives at once, though.
: Calling it “living” is certainly generous.
: Does it ever get tiring?
: Asks the girl who’s been up for over twenty-four hours doing nothing but drawing and reading.
: I like what I like. Is that a problem?
: You’re getting really good.
: At which one? Drawing or reading?
: Drawing. That looks just like her.
: She’s pretty. But I won’t say any more than that because I don’t want to hurt your feelings.
: Does this mean I’m bad at reading then? If drawing is what you were talking about.
: You’re not bad at it.
: But Noriko’s better.
: Noriko’s a prodigy.
: What does that make me then?
: Maya.
: I want to be more than “Maya.”
: You don’t need to be more than Maya.
: I will one day.
: You might love me now, but I’m not naive enough to believe you’ll feel that way forever.
: Maya-
: It’s inevitable. A time will come where temptation will set in or that childhood friend of yours will waltz back into your life and you’ll need to figure out what to do with me.
: I’m not going to do anything with you, though.
: I don’t believe you.
: Well, what can I do to make you believe me?
: A key would be nice.
: What, to the room?
: Your heart.
: That way, any time someone else wanders in, I could come inside and get rid of them without worrying about you locking me out.
: But what if I change the locks?
: Then I’ll know you got tired.
: Like you are right now?
: I’m not done with my drawing yet.
: The hands are always the hardest part.
: Aaaaaand...time!
: Yay! I did it!
: You...certainly did something.
: Could be worse, honestly. Still better than Ryukishi07.
: That’s not the person responsible for bastardizing beloved horses, is it?
: No, and we can all be very thankful for that for a number of reasons.
: Now, everyone will know what Apollo looks like when you talk about him!
: Yasu — I say this with every ounce of love that exists in my heart.
: I want you to burn that as soon as this contest is over.
: Huh?
: Okay! If both Yasu and Maya could make their way over to the...hold on. Where’s Maya?
: I saw her run out a second ago. She took her paper with her too. Art block, maybe? Artist’s block? I’m not sure what it’s called when it doesn’t involve writing.
: Which is unfortunate because she’s actually an exceptional artist. I can try to chase after her and cast “remove curse” if you want to wait for the wizard’s final judgement.
: Please do. Which I’m definitely not just saying because I’d feel wrong handing out a victory to Yasu’s...fantastic drawing of a...d...dragon?
: Ahh. Yes. How could I have been so blind?
: She gave it toes...
: Aren’t they cute?
: They’re...they’re certainly toes, alright.
: I’ll go check the halls for Maya. It’s possible Ami and Ayane caught her.
: Yeah. Go do that, please.
: In the meantime, I’d like to say thanks to all of our dedicated viewers for tuning in to the sixth annual Dorm Wars!
: There’s a much larger subtitle that comes after that, but I don’t remember what it is and I am not sorry about it!
: That’s all for today since we’ve got a special members only contest coming up next! But tune in again tomorrow for five more contests featuring one hosted by yours truly!
: Any last words for our viewers as the tentative winner of our drawing contest, Yasu?
: Just two!
: Praise be!
